issues.title: Direct malloc_usable_size instead of zmalloc_size
issues.description: The rule requires all memory operations to use Redis zmalloc wrappers (zmalloc_size) instead of direct libc functions (malloc_usable_size)

issues.rule_name: Use zmalloc/zfree Wrappers Instead of Direct malloc/free

issues.title: Incorrect memory calculation for QUICKLIST due to wrong denominator
issues.description: In the QUICKLIST encoding branch, the average element size calculation uses `elesize/samples` instead of `elesize/elecount`. This divides the accumulated element size by the number of sampled nodes rather than the total element count in those nodes. Since `elecount` represents the sum of all `node->count` values (the actual number of elements), using `samples` (number of nodes) produces an incorrect average that doesn't represent the true per-element memory usage. This causes the MEMORY USAGE command to return wildly inaccurate values for quicklist-encoded lists.

issues.title: Variable shadowing breaks sampling consistency for STREAM objects
issues.description: A local `samples` variable is declared at line 1319 within the OBJ_STREAM branch, shadowing the outer `samples` variable declared at line 1214. This prevents the outer samples counter from being updated during stream memory calculation. While this doesn't break the stream calculation itself, it violates the function's sampling design pattern where the outer `samples` variable tracks total sampling across all object type branches. This inconsistency could lead to unexpected behavior if the function logic is modified to check or use the outer samples counter after processing.

issues.title: Double-counting last listpack in STREAM memory calculation
issues.description: The stream memory estimation algorithm samples the first N listpacks, computes their average size, and then explicitly adds the last listpack's actual size separately (line 1336). The multiplication at line 1330 should use `(s->rax->numele-1)` to account for all listpacks except the last one, but it incorrectly uses `s->rax->numele` without the subtraction. This causes the last listpack to be counted twice: once in the averaged estimate and once with its actual size, resulting in inflated memory usage reports for streams with more elements than the sample size.

issues.title: Unused variable 'elecount' causes build failure with -Werror
issues.description: The variable 'elecount' is declared and incremented in the QUICKLIST encoding branch (line 1236: 'elecount += node->count') but is never used after the PR changed the calculation from 'elesize/elecount' to 'elesize/samples'. This creates an unused-but-set variable which triggers compiler warnings under -Wall (enabled in Makefile) and causes build failures when compiling with -Werror flag. This violates AGENTS.MD Rule #4 which requires the codebase to compile without warnings when REDIS_CFLAGS="-Werror" is enabled.

issues.title: Internal helper function kvobjComputeSize is not declared static
issues.description: `kvobjComputeSize` appears to be an internal helper used within `src/object.c` (e.g., by the MEMORY USAGE handling code in the same file). Per the rule, such single-compilation-unit helper functions must be declared `static` to avoid exporting unnecessary global symbols.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #14288 - Fix MEMORY USAGE command

structured_output.summary:
The PR renames objectComputeSize() to kvobjComputeSize() and changes it to count the kvobj header and embedded key (via malloc_usable_size on the object) instead of only the value. The MEMORY USAGE call site is updated to pass the kvobj, the stale comments in the hash and list tests are renamed, and a new string test checks lower and upper bounds for a grid of key and value sizes. The goal is right, and the header/key accounting for strings is sound.

The implementation has three real problems beyond the intended change. The header size uses the raw libc malloc_usable_size() instead of zmalloc_size(), which the PR description calls for. On the default jemalloc build that is undefined behavior, and on macOS it likely does not compile. Two aggregate-size formulas were also altered without a rationale: the quicklist average now divides by the number of sampled nodes instead of elements, which inflates list sizes by roughly the elements-per-node factor, and the stream listpack estimate drops the "-1" so the last listpack is counted twice. Neither change is covered by the new tests, which only check string values and the lower bound for INT encoding.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The raw malloc_usable_size() call applied to a zmalloc/jemalloc pointer is a correctness and portability defect that should be fixed before merge. The quicklist divisor and the stream "numele" change each produce wrong MEMORY USAGE values for list and stream keys, and the test additions do not exercise those paths, so they would ship unnoticed. The fix is small, so this is a request for changes, not a rejection of the approach.

architecture.overview:
MEMORY USAGE is handled in src/object.c. The command looks up the key's kvobj with lookupKeyReadWithFlags and then calls a size estimator. Before this PR, that estimator (objectComputeSize) measured only the value's allocations and charged a flat sizeof(robj) per type branch. Since the key-value unification, a kvobj is a single allocation that embeds the key (and possibly the value), so the header-plus-key bytes were not counted. The estimator walks the type and encoding branches (string, list quicklist/listpack, set, zset, hash, stream, module) and sums allocator-reported sizes, sampling up to sample_size elements for aggregate types and extrapolating.

The PR renames the function to kvobjComputeSize, takes a kvobj*, and seeds the total with the allocation size of the kvobj itself. Each branch then adds to asize rather than overwriting it. It also touches the quicklist, stream, and module branches, which changes their arithmetic, not just the header accounting.
steps: Entry point: the MEMORY USAGE subcommand in src/object.c looks up the key with lookupKeyReadWithFlags and returns null for a missing key.
kvobjComputeSize seeds asize with the kvobj's allocation size (header plus embedded key), instead of starting from zero and adding sizeof(*o) per branch.
Per-type branches now add to asize. The string RAW branch adds the sds allocation; the EMBSTR and INT branches add nothing because the value is already in the allocation.
Aggregate branches sample up to sample_size elements and extrapolate. The quicklist branch and the stream listpack branch changed their extrapolation formulas, which is where the regressions are.
Module values delegate to moduleGetMemUsage and now add to the header rather than replacing it.
Tests: the string test checks size bounds for key and value grids; hash and list test comments were renamed. No list or stream bounds test was added.

findings.title: malloc_usable_size() called directly on a zmalloc/jemalloc pointer
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/object.c`, `kvobjComputeSize()` (around line 1217) seeds `asize` with `malloc_usable_size((void *)o)`. That is the libc symbol, but kvobjs are allocated through zmalloc, which on jemalloc builds maps to `je_malloc_usable_size`. Change it to `zmalloc_size((void *)o)` so it uses the same allocator as the rest of the function, and matches the PR description. Check that `zmalloc.h` still provides `zmalloc_size` for the macOS and jemalloc configurations.

findings.title: Quicklist average divides by sampled nodes instead of elements
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/object.c`, in the quicklist branch of `kvobjComputeSize()` (around line 1239), the average-per-element calculation was changed from `elesize/elecount*ql->count` to `elesize/samples*ql->count`. Revert the divisor to `elecount`, which counts elements across the sampled nodes. `samples` counts nodes, so using it inflates list sizes by the elements-per-node factor. Keep `elecount` in use, since it is now the only correct divisor. Add a MEMORY USAGE test for a large list in `tests/unit/type/list.tcl` that checks the result is within a sane bound of the expected size.

findings.title: Stream listpack estimate double-counts the last listpack
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/object.c`, the stream branch of `kvobjComputeSize()` (around line 1330) changed `asize += lpsize * s->rax->numele;` from the original `(numele-1)`. Restore the `-1` so the average is applied only to the first N-1 listpacks, and the last listpack, added separately with `zmalloc_size(ri.data)` right after, is not counted twice. The comment above this block describes the same split. Do not change anything else in the stream branch.

findings.title: New test only covers strings and a loose lower bound, so the list and stream regressions are not caught
findings.body:
The new `MEMORY USAGE - STRINGS` test in `tests/unit/type/string.tcl` checks bounds for string key and value sizes. The bounds are reasonable for kvobj header plus key plus value, and they do test the embedded-key accounting that the PR is about. But:

- The INT branch checks only the lower bound (`min <= used`), so an overestimate there is not caught.
- No list or stream case checks an upper bound. The quicklist and stream bugs above would pass the existing `assert_morethan [memory_usage k] 0` in `tests/unit/type/list.tcl`, which only checks that the result is positive.
- The hash and list test edits only rename comments. They do not add coverage for the changed branches.

A reviewer relying on these tests would believe the aggregate branches are covered when they are not.

::code{file="tests/unit/type/string.tcl" lines="688-688"}

::callout{type="info"}
Add a test that builds a list and a stream with enough elements to hit the sampling path, and asserts that the MEMORY USAGE result stays within a bounded multiple of the expected size. That would have caught both formula regressions above.
findings.fixPrompt: Add regression coverage for the aggregate branches of MEMORY USAGE. In `tests/unit/type/list.tcl`, near the existing `assert_morethan [memory_usage k] 0` check (around line 2245), add an assertion that a list with many small entries reports a size within a bounded multiple of the expected payload, so an inflated quicklist average is caught. Do the same for a stream with several listpacks in `tests/unit/type/stream.tcl`, so the N-1 split is covered. Follow the bounds style used in the new `MEMORY USAGE - STRINGS` test in `tests/unit/type/string.tcl`, and add an upper bound to the INT case there too.
